# MathDB cooperation pilot

[Problem index](README.md) · [New process](../docs/award-process-mathdb.md) · [Legacy process](../docs/award-process.md)

<!-- Generated by scripts/mathdb_pilot.py from mathdb-pilot.json. -->

This register includes **49 distinct problems** for **mathdb**.
The initial pilot includes 21 existing JSP entries and 28 new entries,
JSP-001023–JSP-001050. Existing JSPs, public sources and attribution are retained.

The repository records neither problem levels nor estimated rewards.
Solution, Lean and Exposition have separate review and qualification records;
the legacy shared eligibility flag does not control pilot applications.

The three claim-status columns show public registration independently:
An **empty cell** means no candidate or award is published for that category,
**Candidate** means it appears in the public candidate register, and
**Awarded** means an announced award is recorded. None of these values is
technical/committee approval, a claim-issue state or proof of payment.

**Mapping review:** 46 statement matches checked; 3 unresolved mappings or page statements.
Confirmed means the linked public statement was compared with the selected
problem; it does not accept a proof or determine a reward. Links are shown
without a status prefix; unresolved formulations and page-statement corrections
are recorded in the scope notes and catalog metadata. **Matching page pending**
means no full matching page has been located. Unresolved records do not
authorize automatic handoff; related or alternative pages in the scope notes
are references, not approved replacements.

**Rollout:** `prepared`. Production activation and its UTC effective time must be published and the official MathDB actor/sender configured before automatic claims or success notifications.

For participating problems, we recommend the new process. Other problems
remain on the legacy process until a reviewed scope update and migration
announcement. Preserve original contribution dates and unchanged notice clocks.

## Scope notes

- **JSP-000002 — P versus NP problem:** The linked page identifies P versus NP, but its main statement asserts P=NP and an alleged equivalent formulation asserts P!=NP. These are not equivalent. MathDB must correct the statement to the question whether P equals NP, and the team must confirm correspondence before the agent automatically judges a full solution or hands off a claim. An open-problem tag alone does not establish acceptance of both directions.
- **JSP-001024 — Mirror symmetry conjecture:** Mirror symmetry has several formulations. The current SYZ page is provisional. Alternative for review: [MathDB #374550 — Kontsevich homological mirror symmetry](https://mathdb.com/p/374550/kontsevich-s-homological-mirror-symmetry-conjecture), formulated as an equivalence of Fukaya and derived coherent-sheaf categories. SYZ and homological mirror symmetry are different formulations; the team and MathDB must confirm the intended version before replacing the approved mapping or qualifying a claim.
- **JSP-001041 — Fourier restriction conjecture:** The current page asks for the full range of estimates on general smooth hypersurfaces and remains provisional. Alternative for review: [MathDB #403784 — Fourier restriction conjecture for the sphere](https://mathdb.com/p/403784/fourier-restriction-conjecture-for-the-sphere), which specifies the sphere, dimensions d>=3 and an exponent range. It is a concrete candidate, not an automatic replacement for the broader selected problem. Confirm the intended surface class, dimensions, curvature assumptions and full exponent range with the team and MathDB.

## Sources and maintenance

MathDB page links are the mapping evidence; recent bibliography detection dates
are not substituted for a conjecture's original proposed date.

Maintain [mathdb-pilot.json](mathdb-pilot.json), run
`python3 scripts/mathdb_pilot.py build`, then `python3 scripts/mathdb_pilot.py check`
and the tests described in [record maintenance](../docs/records.md#mathdb-pilot-maintenance).
The pilot page and catalog metadata use the same mapping source. Registration
statuses are generated from the existing candidate/award README registers.
